title: A Taste of Agile
learners_amount: 669 learners have completed this activity in the past 12 months.
star_rating: Average rating of 5 stars by 29 learners in the past 12 months.
description:
About this learning activity

A Taste of Agile is designed to provide a basic awareness of Agile work methods, and how you can use them to change the way you work in academics, on the job, or even in your personal life. The module provides a foundational understanding of the values, principles, practices, and patterns of Agile, and the team dynamics that create success.

 

A Taste of Agile is appropriate for everyone: students, workforce-facing team members, executives, managers, and practitioners.

 

What you’ll learn

After completing this module, you should be able to:

  • Explain the importance of Agile
  • Identify the five Agile values
  • Describe the three Agile principles
  • Describe the seven core Agile practices
  • Identify the three Agile patterns
  • Apply Agile values, principles, and practices in your family, school, or other work

 

Lessons

  1. Introduction to Agile
  2. Core principles of Agile
  3. Practicing Agile
  4. Implementing Agile
  5. Debunking Agile myths
  6. Trends in Agile

learners_amount: 516 learners have completed this activity in the past 12 months.

description:
About this learning activity

Agile Program Fundamentals is designed to help project teams develop the foundational skills to plan, structure, and deliver on programs and projects incrementally and iteratively. This module builds on the foundational awareness from A Taste of Agile and Agile Operations Fundamentals. You will learn the project pattern and receive guidance on recommended practices, tools, and techniques that align to the core Agile values and principles.

 

Agile Program Fundamentals is appropriate for everyone: students, workforce-facing team members, executives, managers, and practitioners.

 

What you’ll learn

After completing this module, you should be able to:

  • Define the term “programs” in a business context
  • Describe the programs pattern
  • Identify the four phases of the programs pattern
  • Describe the application of core practices to program work
  • Apply the Agile method to the programs and projects work you do, whether that be family, school, job, or other types of work

 

Lessons

  1. Adding Agile into the programs pattern
  2. Event phase
  3. Discovery phase
  4. Program funnel phase
  5. Delivery phase

Agile Operations Fundamentals is designed to help operational teams develop the foundational skills to plan, structure, deliver, monitor, and improve on operational activities and processes.
